Atom SDK Getting Started

This section explains how to call an existing Atom algorithm graph through RuntimeService. It focuses on four tasks:

  • list available graphs;

  • run a graph and read its outputs;

  • run one algorithm without creating a graph;

  • change graph parameters and run it again.

Choose Python, C++, or C#.

Before you start

Complete the corresponding language setup in Quick Start. You also need an Atom service address, an existing Runtime graph, and either EPICRAW/file bytes or raw image and point-cloud data.

Choose a graph input mode

Mode Value Input Use when

Normal

"others" or omitted

One or more RuntimeFrame objects

Normal image/point-cloud input, EPICRAW, or data that can be encoded as EPICRAW.

Passive binocular

"passive_bino"

One RuntimePassiveBinoFrame

Passive-binocular EPICRAW3 or three raw input images.

Do not mix the modes. The graph needs a matching EpicProInput configuration and an EpicPro output node.

Common call flow

list_graphs()
load_graph(graph_name)
get_meta_info(graph_name)
set_shared_params(...)       # optional
set_run_params(...)           # optional
run_graph(...)
get_binded_output_value(...)
release_graph(graph_name)

To read a node result, configure its output port as a graph output binding first. RuntimeService cannot query an arbitrary node port directly by node_id.
